title: A customer site's CMS trusts only a per-site HMAC-signed assertion, not bare x-tracy-* headers another site's container could send
steps: S1: Run the Node signer against the shared vectors (packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/access-signature.test.mjs).
S2: Run both PHP verifiers against every shared vector (access-signature-php.test.mjs).

S3: Run the WordPress verifier suite (wordpress-access.test.mjs): forged bare headers, an assertion under another site's key, a wrong-host/method/target/expired assertion, and a replayed nonce each sign nobody in and create no user; a real editor-tier seat reaches the admin.
expect: S1: the signer reproduces every sign vector byte for byte (tests pass, 0 fail).
S2: each verifier returns the expected verdict for every verify vector (0 fail).
S3: every forged/cross-key/expired/replayed case signs nobody in and makes no user; the real seat is signed in as administrator; concurrent replay of one nonce is accepted at most once (0 fail).
evidence: Before this change, code running in one site's web container could POST to http://<otherLabel>-web-1/wp-admin/ (or /administrator/) with forged x-tracy-email/tier/role headers and be minted a WordPress administrator or Joomla Super User of the other site; measured on the local stand 2026-10-26 (attacker-before@evil.test became administrator of p0acc-wpb by DNS name and by IP, and Super Users of p0acc-jma).
fence: Static suites under real PHP (local php or one container) and Node; no stand or network needed — the signer and both verifiers run against shared vectors and WordPress function stubs.
